market_context: United States and general English-speaking market
title: Textured soy protein (TVP): protein, fiber and nutrition

seo.title: TVP nutrition: protein, fiber and calories
seo.meta_description: See how much protein and fiber dry textured vegetable protein provides, what hydration changes, and why dry and cooked weights should not be mixed.

excerpt: Textured vegetable protein is usually defatted soy flour turned into dry porous pieces. A plain current product provides 12 g protein and 4 g fiber per 23 g dry serving; hydration changes weight, not total protein.
content_html:
TVP looks light because most of its water has been removed before it reaches the package. It is a concentrated dry ingredient that is normally rehydrated before eating.

What TVP is

It is commonly made from defatted soy flour. Heat and pressure create a porous structure that absorbs liquid and flavor.

A small dry serving carries a lot of protein

A plain current product lists, per 23 g dry: 80 calories, 12 g protein, 9 g carbohydrate, 4 g fiber and 0 g fat. Scaled to 100 g dry, that is about 52 g protein and 17 g fiber.

Hydration changes concentration, not total protein

Hydrate 23 g dry TVP and the finished batch still has about 12 g protein. Water simply makes it heavier.

What defatting and seasoning change

The example is made from defatted soy flour, so it lists 0 g fat per serving. Tofu and tempeh retain more natural soybean fat.

Plain TVP here lists 0 mg sodium. Prepared crumbles and sauces can be much saltier.

Dry and hydrated values answer different questions

Comparing 100 g of dry TVP with 100 g of tofu or cooked meat exaggerates the impression of concentration because one sample contains very little water. If 23 g of dry TVP hydrates to roughly 60–70 g, those 12 g of protein are still there; they are simply distributed through more total weight.

For meal planning, it is therefore more useful to start with the dry amount you actually use. For comparing nutrient density between products, the foods need to be put in comparable states—dry with dry or prepared with prepared—before drawing conclusions.

Track the dry amount you started with, then divide the batch among servings. That avoids mixing dry and hydrated weights.

faq.question: How much protein is in TVP?
faq.answer: 12 g per 23 g dry in the reference product, about 52 g/100 g dry.

faq.question: Does hydration remove protein?
faq.answer: No. It adds water and lowers protein per 100 g, not total batch protein.

faq.question: Does TVP contain fiber?
faq.answer: Yes, 4 g per 23 g dry serving here.

faq.question: Is TVP low in fat?
faq.answer: Defatted TVP can be; this product lists 0 g per serving.
